text:
carmen: hey — customer sent us a request_id 84f3c2a7 and says they got a 500. i tried the Console but can't find any raw lines for that id. any quick pointers?

devon: do you have the full header value? sometimes we strip prefixes. try searching for just the last 8 chars or the trace id if they gave it. also check the edge proxy logs first.

carmen: pasted what they sent: x-request-id: 2026-84f3c2a7

kai: if it's the console, use the Logs -> Live view and search for `84f3c2a7` with quotes. but often Console's index doesn't include the full header. i usually fall back to stern on the edge pods.

kai: example stern command i run:

```bash
stern -n prod "edge-.*" --since 10m | grep 84f3c2a7
```

kai: if you're hunting historical logs (not live), use our log search query: `json.payload.x_request_id:"84f3c2a7" OR message:%2284f3c2a7%22` (escape quotes in the Console).

carmen: thanks. any tips when trace links exist but they don't show raw lines? the Traces view has the span but "view logs" link is empty.

devon: that usually means the span's service didn't tag the request id in the logged payload, so the trace->log correlation failed. check the span attributes for `x_request_ref` or `request_ref` — we map that to logs at ingest time.

infra-bot: Reminder: when trace->log link is missing, routing may have dropped the `x-request-ref`. See runbook: https://console.redwood.internal/runbooks/trace-log-correlation (note: internal link).

hana: if you want an automated lookup i can run a quick correlate job — ping me the full request id and timestamp window and i'll chase through the edge + gateway + app pods. otherwise try this multi-step CLI approach: search edge logs (stern), if found, take pod+ts and then `kubectl logs <pod> -c app --since=1h | sed -n '1,200p' | grep 84f3c2a7` to capture full request payload.

carmen: really helpful, thanks. i'll try stern first and if nothing, i'll @hana with the id + approx time. appreciate it :thumbsup:
